prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an indoor salon-like room where the camera wearer's own raised left arm, right hand, hairdryer, and round brush in the foreground are brightest at roughly 0.2–0.5 m (within arm's reach), positioned directly above and in front of a seated person's head and upper torso at about 0.5–0.8 m below the viewpoint. Across the tiled floor in the background (roughly 3–5 m away and 2.5–4 m behind the foreground person), a standing child near a blue salon chair/desk, a seated adult about 0.5–1 m to the child's left, a black rolling cart to the right, and a brick fireplace structure further right are rendered in dark grey tones. Across the five frames, the wearer's left arm and the hairdryer shift from lower-left in frame 1 to high overhead in frame 2, then angle down toward the right in frames 3–5 as the dryer nozzle approaches the top of the seated client's head, partially occluding the background child and seated adult in frames 2–4 while the client's lower body and the wearer's torso remain out of view below the bottom edge. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the depth planes of the dark hairdryer, its thin hanging cord, and the dark hair of the client which otherwise blend visually, and shows the continuous receding slope of the floor. However, the map is unreliable where the hairdryer nozzle and the client's hair merge into a single uniform brightness in frames 3–5, and in the upper-left background above 4 m where furniture and the seated person flatten into nearly indistinguishable black silhouettes.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete regions across the scene, identifying the seated client in the lower-center foreground (0.5–0.8 m away, facing away from and looking down relative to the camera wearer), the wearer's raised left arm entering from the bottom-left (0.2–0.4 m away), the black rolling cart at 2.5–3 m in the upper-center, and the distant child and seated adult at 3–4.5 m in the upper-left (both facing roughly rightward/away from the wearer and within arm's reach of the blue salon furniture). Across the five frames, the foreground masks reconfigure as the wearer's left arm and hairdryer sweep overhead in frame 2—occluding the distant child—and descend rightwards in frames 3–5, while the seated client remains stationary below and only the wearer's hands, hairdryer, brush, and the client's head are within the wearer's arm's reach. While the map provides sharp boundary contours for the wearer's foreground arm and consistently tracks the rolling cart ('chair') at ~3 m across all five frames, it is heavily unreliable in its semantic class labels and temporal consistency. Specifically, it merges the wearer's arm and hairdryer into a single 'person' mask in frame 2, mislabels the hairdryer and client's head as 'backpack' and 'laptop' in frame 3, drops the foreground client mask completely in frame 4, and misclassifies the client's head/dryer as a brown 'person' mask containing a tiny 'cell phone' at the bottom where the brush and right hand are in frame 5. Furthermore, the brick fireplace on the right, the blue chair at the bottom-left (~1.2 m away), and the distant background sofa are completely unsegmented throughout.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the sequence, detecting only a magenta left-hand skeleton for the camera wearer at roughly 0.3–0.4 m in the upper-left foreground of frames 3, 4, and 5, plus a distorted yellow body-torso polygon in the lower-center foreground of frame 4 (~0.6 m away). In frames 3 and 4, the magenta hand skeleton shows the wrist on the left with fingers extending rightward and slightly upward as the hand grips the hairdryer handle above the seated client, then shifts lower and tilts downward to the right in frame 5 as the wearer's arm lowers and rotates the dryer. When present, these keypoints make the exact articulation of the wearer's thumb and curled fingers around the hairdryer grip easier to read than in the motion-blurred RGB frames. However, the map is highly unreliable because it completely misses all body and hand skeletons in frames 1 and 2, fails to detect the wearer's right hand holding the brush at the bottom edge (~0.4–0.5 m away) in any frame, and misses the distant standing child and seated adult (3–4.5 m away) entirely. Additionally, the yellow body skeleton that briefly appears in frame 4 hallucinatedly bridges the hairdryer and the seated client's head and shoulders without indicating true anatomical orientation, leaving the facing directions and poses of all three other people in the room unrepresented.
